source_text: Ὢ πόσα δύναται πίστις καὶ τὸ ἐξομολογῆσαι υἱὸν ἀληθινὸν εἶναι τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μὴ κτίσμα τὸν μονογενῆ θεὸν λόγον. 30.9 οὐκ ἐδίστασεν Πέτρος σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι θεὸν ἐπὶ γῆς ἐμφιλοχωροῦντα ὁρῶν· τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὅτι «σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι»· 30.10 ἐπέγνω δὲ τὸν συμφυᾶ καὶ συναΐδιον κλάδον τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐτίμησεν ἐν τούτῳ τὴν ἀποκαλύψασαν αὐτῷ αὐτογενῆ καὶ ἄναρχον ῥίζαν· ἐπίστευσεν αὐτοῦ τῇ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα τῆς θεότητος ἑνότητι· 30.11 ἐμακαρίσθη ὑπὸ τοῦ μόνου μακαρίου δεσπότου. ᾠκοδομήθησαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν ταύτην αἱ ἐκκλησίαι, ὧντινων «πύλαι ᾅδου», τουτέστιν αἱρετικῶν συλλογισμοί, οὐ περιγένωνται· 30.12 ἐνεχειρίσθη τὰς κλεῖς τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα τοῖς μὲν πιστεύουσιν–ὡς αὐτὸς Πέτρος ἀρτίως ἀποκρινάμενος φαίνεται καὶ ὡς παρὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ σὺν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἤκουσεν ἀποστόλοις· «βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύ ματος»– ἀνοίξῃ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ· 30.13 τοῖς δὲ μὴ οὕτω δοξάζουσιν τὴν τρισμακαρίαν καὶ εὐκταιοτάτην εἴσοδον ἀποκλείσῃ. 30.14 αὐτῷ γὰρ τούτῳ, ᾧ ἐμακαρίσθη, αὐτὸς ἐπὶ τῇδε τῇ δόξῃ ἐδέχθη, ὡς οἱ ἀπεναντίως λέγοντες 35 κατεψέχθησάν τε καὶ ἀπεβλήθησαν. 30.15 Ἀληθεύσας δὴ οὖν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διωμολογηκὼς αὐτόν, τουτέστιν 30.15 γνήσιον καὶ ὁμοούσιον, παραπλήσια ἤκουσεν· Βὰρ Ἰωνᾶ, ὁ ἑρμηνεύεται· υἱὲ Ἰωνᾶ. 30.16 οὐκ ἦν δὲ πάντως ἑτεροούσιος τῷ τεκόντι αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος. 30.17 Πρὸς τούτοις ἔλαβεν ἐξουσίαν, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ πάντες δι' αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀπαγορεύειν τοῖς πταίουσιν, ἀλλὰ δέχεσθαι μετανοοῦντας. 30.18 οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀναμάρτητος, εἰ μὴ ὁ ταύτην ἐπιτρέψας τῷ Πέτρῳ τὴν αὐθεντείαν, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν· «ὃ ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς». 30.19 ἔρριψεν ἔκτοτε τὴν Ναυάτου καὶ Σαββατίου ἀπανθρωπίαν· 30.20 Τοῖς προκειμένοις δὲ αὖ ἕπεται καὶ Παῦλος Γαλάταις γράφων· «ὅτε δὲ εὐδόκησεν ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοί», 30.21 καὶ Κολοσσαεῦσιν· «εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ πατρὶ τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν μερίδα τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί· ὃς ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ σκότους καὶ μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν», 30.22 καὶ Κορινθίοις· «πιστὸς ὁ θεός, δι' οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν», 30.23 καὶ Ἐφεσίοις· «καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐηγγελίσατο εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ εἰρήνην τοῖς ἐγγύς, ὅτι δι' αὐτοῦ ἔχομεν τὴν προσαγωγὴν οἱ ἀμφότεροι ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα». 31.ν Περὶ τοῦ μὴ εἶναι τέλος τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ μονογενοῦς. 31.1 Καὶ ὥστε αἱρετικοὺς λέγοντας, ὅτι μετὰ τὴν γενικὴν ἀνάστασιν ὁ υἱὸς παραδιδόναι μέλλει τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ πατρί, καταισχύνεσθαι, κηρύττουσι τὸ κράτος τοῦ υἱοῦ εἶναι ἀτελεύτητον οὑτωσί· 31.2 Γαβριὴλ μὲν παρὰ Λουκᾷ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν θεοτόκον· «καὶ δώσει», φησίν, «αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὸν θρόνον ∆αυῒδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, καὶ τῆς βασι λείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος». 31.3 καὶ μάλα ἀληθῶς· εἰ γὰρ ἀποκαθίστησιν, ἐν ποίᾳ αὐτοῦ βασιλείᾳ καὶ πότε συμβασιλεύσομεν αὐτῷ; 31.4 Παῦλος δὲ γράφων πρὸς Ἐφεσίους μέν· «πᾶς πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης, ὅς ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης, οὐκ ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ». πάντως δὲ λέγει τὴν μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν. 31.5 πότε οὖν λοιπὸν κατ' ἐκείνους παραδίδωσι τὴν βασιλείαν; 31.6 Πρὸς δὲ Τιμόθεον τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἐπιστολῇ· «διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ μέλλοντος κρί νειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ· κήρυξον τὸν λόγον». 31.7 σαφὲς δέ, ὅτι βασιλείαν λέγει ἣν ἔχει ἀδιαίρετον καὶ ἀδιάδοχον μετὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος νῦν τε καὶ εἰς τὸν μέλλοντα αἰῶνα. 31.8 Πρὸς δὲ Ἑβραίους· «καὶ πρὸς μὲν τοὺς ἀγγέλους λέγει· ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα· πρὸς δὲ τὸν υἱόν· ὁ θρόνος σου, ὁ θεός, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος». 31.9 ∆αυῒδ δὲ ἐν μδʹ ψαλμῷ· «ὁ θρόνος σου, ὁ θεός, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος· ῥάβδος εὐθύτητος ἡ ῥάβδος τῆς βασιλείας σου. ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀδικίαν. διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέν σε, θεέ, ὁ θεός σου ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου». 31.10 ἄθρει καὶ αὖθις τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ ἀπέραντον καὶ τὴν θεότητα ἄναρχον.
pass_a_gloss: 30.8 Oh, how many things faith can do, and to confess the only-begotten God Word to be true Son of God and not a creature! 30.9 Peter did not waver through flesh and blood, seeing God gladly dwelling on earth; for this is [the meaning of] 'flesh and blood did not reveal [it] to you'. 30.10 And he recognized the co-natural and co-eternal branch of God; he honoured in this the self-existent and beginningless root that revealed [him] to him; he believed in his oneness of Godhead toward the Father; 30.11 he was declared blessed by the only blessed Master. The churches were built on this rock, which 'gates of Hades', that is, syllogisms of heretics, shall not overcome; 30.12 he was entrusted with the keys of the heavens, so that for those who believe (as Peter himself is seen to have answered just now and as he heard from Christ with the other apostles: 'baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit') he might open in the kingdom of God, 30.13 and for those who do not glorify thus he might shut the thrice-blessed and most prayed-for entrance. 30.14 For by this very thing by which he was declared blessed, he himself was received into this glory, as those speaking oppositely [page number 35] were both blamed and cast off. 30.15 So having spoken truly in having confessed him Son of God, that is [the repeated number 30.15 is debris] genuine and of one substance, he heard similar things: Bar-Jonah, which is interpreted: son of Jonah. 30.16 And Peter was not at all of another substance from the one who begot him. 30.17 Besides these he received authority, rather also all through him, not to renounce those who stumble, but to receive [them] repenting. 30.18 For no one is sinless, except the one who entrusted this authority to Peter; for this is: 'whatever you [plural] loose on the earth will be loosed in the heavens'. 30.19 He threw away from then on the inhumanity of Novatian and Sabbatius. 30.20 And Paul too in turn follows the things set out, writing to the Galatians: 'but when God, who separated me from my mother's womb, was well pleased to reveal his Son in me', 30.21 and to the Colossians: 'giving thanks to the Father who made us sufficient for the portion of the lot of the saints in the light; who rescued us out of the authority of the darkness and transferred [us] into the kingdom of the Son of his love, in whom we have the redemption, the forgiveness of sins', 30.22 and to the Corinthians: 'faithful is God, through whom you were called into fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord', 30.23 and to the Ephesians: 'and having come he preached peace to you who were far and peace to those near, because through him we both have the access in one Spirit to the Father'. 31.ν [Chapter title:] About there not being an end of the kingdom of the only-begotten. 31.1 And so that heretics saying that after the general resurrection the Son is going to hand over the kingdom to the Father may be put to shame, they proclaim the might of the Son to be endless thus: 31.2 Gabriel in Luke, announcing good news to the God-bearer: 'and the Lord God', he says, 'will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Israel into the ages, and of his kingdom there will not be an end'. 31.3 And very truly; for if he gives [it] back, in what kingdom of his and when shall we reign together with him? 31.4 And Paul, writing to the Ephesians: 'every fornicator or unclean or greedy person, who is an idolater, does not have inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and God'. And he certainly speaks of the [kingdom] after the resurrection. 31.5 When then, after all, according to those men, does he hand over the kingdom? 31.6 And to Timothy in the second letter: 'I solemnly charge before God and Christ Jesus, who is about to judge living and dead, and [by] his appearing and his kingdom: preach the word'. 31.7 And it is clear that he speaks of the kingdom which he has undivided and without succession with the Father and the Holy Spirit, both now and into the coming age. 31.8 And to the Hebrews: 'and to the angels he says: the one making his angels spirits and his ministers a flame of fire; but to the Son: your throne, O God, into the age of the age'. 31.9 And David in the 44th psalm (Greek numbering; Psalm 45 in English): 'your throne, O God, into the age of the age; a rod of straightness the rod of your kingdom. You loved righteousness and hated injustice. Because of this, O God, your God anointed you with oil of exultation beyond your partners'. 31.10 Look again at his kingdom boundless and his Godhead beginningless.
pass_b_english: Oh, how much faith can do, and the confession that the only-begotten God the Word is the true Son of God and not a creature!

Peter did not waver through flesh and blood when he saw God gladly dwelling on earth; that is what “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you” (Matthew 16:17) means. He recognized the branch of God that shares his nature and his eternity. In him he honoured the self-existent root without beginning that had revealed him. He believed in the oneness of Godhead that the Son has with the Father. He was declared blessed by the only blessed Master.

On this rock the churches have been built, and “the gates of Hades” (Matthew 16:18), that is, the syllogisms of heretics, shall not overcome them. He was entrusted with the keys of the heavens, so that for those who believe he might open the way in the kingdom of God, believing as Peter himself plainly answered just now, and as he heard from Christ together with the other apostles: “baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19); and that for those who do not give glory in this way he might shut the thrice-blessed and most longed-for entrance. For by the very thing for which he was called blessed, he himself was received into this glory, while those who say the opposite were rebuked and cast out.

So, having spoken the truth in confessing him the Son of God, that is, genuine and of one substance, he heard the like in return: Bar-Jonah, which is translated “son of Jonah.” And Peter was certainly not of another substance from the one who begot him.

Besides this he received authority (or rather all received it through him) not to give up on those who fall, but to receive them when they repent. For no one is without sin except the one who entrusted this authority to Peter. That is the meaning of: “Whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in the heavens” (Matthew 18:18). From then on he cast away the inhumanity of Novatian and Sabbatius.

Paul in turn follows what has been set out, writing to the Galatians: “But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb, was pleased to reveal his Son in me” (Galatians 1:15-16); and to the Colossians: “Giving thanks to the Father, who has made us fit for a share in the inheritance of the saints in the light. He rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins” (Colossians 1:12-14); and to the Corinthians: “God is faithful, through whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord” (1 Corinthians 1:9); and to the Ephesians: “And he came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near; for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father” (Ephesians 2:17-18).
That the kingdom of the Only-begotten has no end.

And to put to shame the heretics who say that after the general resurrection the Son will hand over the kingdom to the Father, the Scriptures proclaim that the dominion of the Son has no end. They do so thus. Gabriel in Luke, bringing the good news to the God-bearer: “And the Lord God,” he says, “will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Israel for ever, and of his kingdom there will be no end” (Luke 1:32-33). And very truly so. For if he gives the kingdom back, in what kingdom of his, and when, shall we reign with him?

And Paul, writing to the Ephesians: “Every fornicator or unclean or greedy person, that is, an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God” (Ephesians 5:5). He certainly means the kingdom after the resurrection. When, then, on their view, does he hand over the kingdom?

And to Timothy in the second letter: “I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom: preach the word” (2 Timothy 4:1-2). It is clear that he means the kingdom which he holds undivided and without successor with the Father and the Holy Spirit, both now and in the age to come.

And to the Hebrews: “Of the angels he says, ‘He makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire’; but of the Son, ‘Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever’” (Hebrews 1:7-8). And David in the forty-fifth Psalm: “Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; a sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore, O God, your God has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions” (Psalm 45:6-7). See once more: his kingdom is boundless and his Godhead without beginning.

lemmas.gloss: grown together, of one nature with

choices.issue: Old draft garbled and broke quotations
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English turned the opening exclamation into 'the confession that the true Son is God', made the root 'revealed to him' (ἀποκαλύψασαν is active: the root that revealed him), made those who do not glorify 'glorify the entrance' (the entrance is what Peter shuts), quoted 'whatever you bind' where Didymus has 'whatever you loose' (λύσητε), had 'Gabriel, being announced by Luke' and 'to be ashamed of heretics' in 31.1-31.2, cut Colossians 1:12-14 off at 'in whom...' and began a new paragraph with 'Therefore', and used the fillers [being], [he], [the kingdom] and 'unto' outside a quotation. References: abbreviations written in full; Galatians 1:15 widened to 1:15-16 (the quotation ends in 1:16), Colossians 1:13 to 1:12-14, 2 Timothy 4:1 to 4:1-2, 'Heb 1:7, 8' to Hebrews 1:7-8; the stray (Matthew 16:17) after 'Bar Jonah' removed; Greek Psalm 44 rendered 'forty-fifth Psalm' (Psalm 45:6-7).

choices.english: Oh, how much faith can do
choices.why: Exclamation with δύναται; the section opens here because the preceding paragraph number (30.8) ends the previous section.

choices.term: οὐκ ἐδίστασεν Πέτρος σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι
choices.english: Peter did not waver through flesh and blood
choices.why: The dative goes with the verb, as Didymus' gloss shows ('that is what “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you” means'): human reasoning did not make Peter doubt. Reading 'God in flesh and blood' would lose that link.
The verb means to linger in a place one loves; 'indwelling' (old draft) lost the warmth.
αὐτογενής of the Father means having being from himself, not 'self-begotten' in a sense that would imply a begetting.

choices.term: ἀνοίξῃ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ
choices.english: he might open the way in the kingdom of God
choices.why: The verb has no expressed object; the object of the paired verb ἀποκλείσῃ is 'the entrance', so 'the way' is the least English needs. Not bracketed because it supplies no new claim. The parenthesis on Peter's answer is moved after the verb so the sentence can be read aloud.

choices.english: he heard the like in return: Bar-Jonah
choices.why: Didymus' point: Peter called Jesus 'Son of God' and was himself called 'son of Jonah', a son of one substance with his father; so the Son is of one substance with the Father.
Greek writers call the Roman schismatic Novatian 'Ναυάτος'; Sabbatius led a later Novatianist split. Both refused readmission to the lapsed, hence 'inhumanity'.
Literal rendering of the title of Mary; kept as a title, not expanded.
The plural verb has no expressed subject; the list that follows (Gabriel, Paul, David) shows it is the scriptural witnesses. The old draft's bracketed [he] was wrong in number.

choices.term: ἔχρισέν σε, θεέ, ὁ θεός σου
choices.english: therefore, O God, your God has anointed you
choices.why: Didymus' text has the vocative θεέ, which the usual LXX lacks; it strengthens his point that the Son is addressed as God, so it is kept.
Split words (πνεύ ματος, βασι λείας, κρί νειν) read as single words; the page number '35' in 30.14 and the repeated paragraph number '30.15' inside 30.15 are skipped.
